name: Question 5
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t)-y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)={y}^{2}(t)-x(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives all equilibrium points of the system of differential equations above?
worked_solution:
The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y=0 \\ {y}^{2}-x=0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the first equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y=0\,⇒\,y=2x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $y$ into the second equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-x & =0 \\ (2x)^{2}-x & =0 \\ 4{x}^{2}-x & =0 \\ x(4x-1) & =0 \\ x & =0,\text{ }\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $y:$

- For $x=0,$ we get $y=2\cdot 0=0.$

- For $x=\frac{1}{4},$ we get $y=2\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{2}.$

Therefore, the equilibrium points are

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

{x′(t)=2x(t)−y(t)y′(t)=y2(t)−x(t) Which of the following gives all equilibrium points of the system of differential equations above?

a
[12] only
b
[00] only
c
[012] and [−1412]
d
[−1412] only
e
[00] and [1412]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system x′(t)=f(x,y) are the points for which f(x,y)=0. So, we get the following system of equations: {2x−y=0y2−x=0

Now, we solve the first equation for y: 2x−y=0⇒y=2x

Next, we substitute y into the second equation y2−x=0(2x)2−x=04x2−x=0x(4x−1)=0x=0, 14.

Now, we compute y:

  • For x=0, we get y=2⋅0=0.

  • For x=14, we get y=2⋅14=12.

Therefore, the equilibrium points are [00]and[1412].
